RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Electrical and Electronic Equipment Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder
and recorded in the schedule.

Where an insured item of property is destroyed or damaged, the insurer
indemnifies the cost of putting it back. The normal arrangement is reinstatement
in the same kind and quality, to a condition as new, on an index-linked
reinstatement basis with an enhancement. A range of consequential expenses
triggered by a loss event is also carried, within the limits agreed for each
head.

This contract indemnifies physical damage to insured property only. It is not a
liability contract, not a service, maintenance or extended-warranty arrangement,
and not a contract for the procurement of goods or services as such.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.
They appear in three places in these conditions: as general exclusions applying
across the contract, within the provisions on individual perils and types of
damage, and within the description of the insured property.

Repair cost - the outlay that is directed at making good the physical damage
caused by the insured event on the affected item itself. Outlay that pursues any
other purpose is not a repair cost, however it may be described or invoiced.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the itemised labour and materials
of a repair or replacement: carriage, freight, delivery, packaging, transport,
call-out and travel, fitting, mounting, commissioning, configuration,
administration, handling and comparable items.

Sub-limit - a monetary ceiling that applies within the sum insured to a defined
class of property or to a defined head of cost. Where a sub-limit applies, the
class of property or head of cost is indemnified only up to that ceiling; the
excess is borne by the policyholder.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before,
during and after an insured event.

Secured lenders - creditors whose claim is secured by a charge registered
against the property. The interests of secured lenders enjoy statutory
protection.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or
lost as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1).

2.3 The fire group defined

2.3.1 Fire
A combustion that has started without a hearth intended for it, or that has
escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of spreading under its own power.

2.3.2 Lightning strike
The direct passage of a lightning discharge onto property.

2.3.3 Overvoltage caused by lightning
Damage arising through overvoltage, overcurrent or short circuit, brought about
by a lightning discharge or by other atmospheric electricity, in insured
electrical installations and appliances.

Cover under this heading extends to individually replaceable electrical and
electronic appliances and to assemblies of such appliances, including
audio-visual, audio-reproduction, communication and comparable entertainment
equipment, whether free-standing, connected to a fixed installation or mounted
to it, insofar as they are located within the insured building.

Indemnity for the class of property described in the preceding paragraph is
subject in every case to the appliance sub-limit agreed in the schedule, applied
per insured event and in the aggregate across all appliances and all invoices
relating to that event. Where the loss on that class of property exceeds the
sub-limit, indemnity is confined to the sub-limit and the balance is borne by
the policyholder. Within that sub-limit, indemnity is further governed by 7.1.9
(no improvement on the pre-loss standard).

2.3.4 Explosion and deflagration
Both are suddenly running force events resting on the tendency of gases or
vapours to expand. They differ only in the intensity of that force.

2.3.5 Implosion
A sudden, unforeseen collapse of a hollow body under external overpressure
resulting from an internal underpressure.

2.3.6 Impact or crash of an aircraft
The impact or crash of an aircraft is covered, and equally that of its parts or
its cargo.

2.3.7 Vehicle impact
The impact of a road, rail or water-borne vehicle against insured property is
covered, as is the impact of parts or cargo of such a vehicle. Not covered is
damage caused by a vehicle whose keeper or driver is the policyholder or an
occupant of the building.

2.3.8 Scorching
Scorch damage arising out of one of the events in 2.3.1 to 2.3.7 is covered.
Scorch damage from any other cause is covered up to [amount].

2.3.9 Smoke and soot
Smoke and soot damage arising out of one of the events in 2.3.1 to 2.3.8 is
covered. Damage arising from the gradual action of smoke or soot is not covered.

2.3.10 Damage excluded within the fire group
Not covered:
  (a) damage caused by earthquake, irrespective of any contributing causes;
  (b) damage to internal combustion engines caused by the explosions occurring
      inside the machine's combustion chamber, and damage arising at the
      switching elements of electrical switches through the gas pressure
      occurring inside them, unless the consequence of an insured fire event;
  (c) damage to electrical or electronic appliances caused by wear, ageing,
      internal defect, operating error or failure of a component, where no
      insured peril under 2.1 acted on the appliance.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.1 The escape of water peril covers escape of water damage, fracture damage
to pipework inside buildings and fracture damage to pipework outside buildings.

2.4.2 Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended
purpose from pipes of the water supply or hoses connected to them, from other
installations connected to those pipes, from heating or air-conditioning
systems, from water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems, or from water beds
or aquaria.

2.4.3 Covered inside buildings is frost-related and other fracture damage to the
pipework of the water, gas, heating, air-conditioning, extinguishing and
rainwater-drainage installations, and frost-related fracture damage to the
sanitary fittings, valves, radiators, boilers and comparable parts of those
systems.

2.4.4 Covered outside buildings is frost-related and other fracture damage to
supply pipes, insofar as the policyholder bears the risk for those pipes and
insofar as they serve the supply of insured buildings or are situated on the
insured site. Indemnity is limited per insured event to the amounts agreed for
those purposes.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

2.5.1 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength. Hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice.

2.5.2 Only damage arising from the direct action of storm or hail on insured
property, on buildings in which insured property is located, or on buildings
structurally joined to them, is covered, together with damage caused by objects
thrown onto them by storm or hail.

2.5.3 The further natural hazards are flood, backing-up of water, earthquake,
ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as
customarily defined and each available only in combination with a peril under
2.1(a), (b) or (c1).


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract. Charges which combine an indemnity for physical damage to
property with the assumption or handling of a liability risk fall outside this
cover in their entirety unless the physical-damage element is separately
itemised and separately priced.

3.1.5 Service, maintenance and warranty arrangements
Outlay arising from a service, maintenance, inspection, extended-warranty,
support or comparable ongoing arrangement, and any charge for placing,
registering, administering or executing an order under such an arrangement, is
not indemnifiable. This applies irrespective of whether the arrangement was
entered into on the occasion of an insured event, and irrespective of whether
the charge is raised by the trade carrying out covered work.

3.2 Exclusions within the fire group

See 2.3.10.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

Damage caused by splash or cleaning water; dry rot and house-rot fungi;
groundwater, surface water, flood, precipitation or a backing-up brought about
by these; earthquake, snow load, avalanche or volcanic eruption; ground
subsidence or landslip not caused by escaping water; the perils of the fire
group; the opening of sprinklers on account of fire, pressure testing or works;
and storm or hail, is not covered. Damage to buildings or parts of buildings
that are not ready for occupation is not covered.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

Damage caused by storm surge; by the penetration of precipitation or dirt
through openings that were not properly closed; by groundwater save where it
emerged at the surface as a result of precipitation or overflow; by the perils of
the fire group, save where triggered by an insured earthquake; and by drought or
desiccation, is not covered.

3.5 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not constitute a
repair cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is governed by
7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the buildings identified in the schedule, their
building components, their building accessories, terraces on the insured site
that directly adjoin the building, and further site installations.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground, capable of affording
protection against external influences and intended for predominantly
residential use.

4.2.2 Building components
Items incorporated into a building that have lost their independence through
their firm connection with it, together with the fitting-out elements of the
dwelling.

4.2.3 Building accessories
Movable items located inside the building or attached to its exterior which
serve the upkeep of the insured building or its predominant intended purpose.

4.2.4 Electrical and electronic appliances
Electrical and electronic appliances and assemblies of such appliances are
insured against the peril under 2.3.3 only, and only within the appliance
sub-limit under 2.3.3. They are treated as a single class of property for the
purposes of that sub-limit, irrespective of the number of appliances affected,
the number of trades involved or the number of invoices rendered.

An appliance is regarded as affected only where physical damage to that
appliance is established by the loss investigation. Appliances which are
exchanged, upgraded, added or reconfigured on the occasion of the loss without
having been themselves damaged are not insured property.

4.2.5 Terraces and further site installations
Terraces are paved surfaces intended for occupation in the open air. Further
site installations are the items firmly connected with the ground and soil of
the insured site listed in the schedule.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components, including a permanently
      connected electricity storage installation;
  (b) items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner at that person's own expense and at that person's own
      risk, unless co-insured under 4.4;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs, and the restoration, migration,
      re-licensing or re-configuration of software, media content, user accounts
      and comparable intangible items;
  (d) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace a
      damaged insured item of the same kind and intended purpose.

4.4 Optionally insurable

By way of departure from 4.3(b), items subsequently incorporated by a tenant or
condominium owner can be co-insured where this is agreed.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel or parcels on which
the insured building stands.

4.6 Condominium and part-ownership units

Where the contract is with an association of condominium owners and the insurer
is wholly or partly released from liability on account of the conduct of
individual owners, it remains obliged to pay the remaining owners in respect of
their separate property and their shares in the common property. The remaining
owners may claim indemnity for the co-ownership share concerned where the
additional indemnity is applied to reinstating the common property; the owner
concerned must reimburse the insurer. These provisions apply correspondingly to
part-ownership units.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set out
in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the covered
settlement, irrespective of the number of trades or invoices involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) debris removal and demolition costs;
  (b) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (c) costs of lost water, gas and heating oil, and of electricity lost from
      storage installations;
  (d) hotel costs;
  (e) costs of returning early from a holiday.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it.
This list is exhaustive. A head of cost that does not fall within it, and that is
not a repair cost within the meaning of 7.1.7, is not insured.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Debris removal and demolition
Costs incurred in clearing away and demolishing insured property, including
removing the remains of that property, transporting them to the nearest disposal
site, depositing them and destroying them.

5.2.2 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting other property, where those
measures serve to reinstate or replace insured property. This head does not
extend to the carriage, freight, delivery or transport of newly procured
property to the insured location.

5.2.3 Lost water, gas, heating oil and stored electricity
Costs arising because these escaped or were lost contrary to their intended
purpose as a result of an insured event, capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.4 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation where the dwelling permanently occupied by the
policyholder has become uninhabitable and confining themselves to a habitable
part of it cannot reasonably be expected, reimbursed only to the extent that
they exceed the indemnity payable for rental value and only where indemnity
cannot be claimed under another insurance contract, up to [amount] per day for a
maximum of [number] days.

5.2.5 Early return from holiday
Additional travel costs arising because the policyholder, or a person living
with them in the same household, breaks off a holiday trip prematurely on
account of a significant insured event, in a reasonable amount and capped at
[amount] per insured event.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent or terminated the tenancy on account of an insured
event, and the locally customary rental value of residential premises occupied
by the policyholder itself where use cannot reasonably be expected, in each case
including the running service charges in the sense of tenancy law.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.

5.5 Commercially used premises

For commercially used premises, insurance of loss of rent or of the locally
customary rental value can be agreed.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. The insurable
value determined for the building applies equally to building accessories,
terraces and further site installations.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

6.2.1 What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the buildings
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event.

6.2.2 Two elements are built into that value: additional costs arising from
public-law restrictions on reinstatement, and price increases arising between the
occurrence of the insured event and reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.2.3 The insurer tracks the cover against the development of building costs.

6.2.4 The reinstatement basis under this Part does not displace a sub-limit.
Where a class of property or a head of cost carries a sub-limit, the sub-limit
determines the ceiling of the indemnity for that class or head even where the
reinstatement cost demonstrably exceeds it.

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted
    or delayed

For buildings that are not reinstated, or are reinstated late, only the
index-linked current value with enhancement is insured - the enhanced new-build
value at the time of the insured event, less depreciation for age and wear.

6.4 Market value for permanently devalued buildings

For buildings designated for demolition, or otherwise permanently devalued, only
the achievable sale price excluding the land share is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and fit-out, the use, other agreed features material to the premium
calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of a
construction price index for residential buildings and a collectively agreed wage
index for the construction sector, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings - the locally customary reinstatement costs at the
      time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings and other damaged property - the necessary repair
      costs at the time of the insured event, together with any diminution in
      value the repair does not offset, capped at the insurable value;
  (c) for destroyed or lost other property - the replacement price for property
      of the same kind and quality in new condition at the time of the insured
      event.

Where the property concerned belongs to a class carrying a sub-limit, the
indemnity under (b) or (c) is in every case confined to that sub-limit.

7.1.2 Where technically still usable substance may not be used for reinstatement
because of public-law requirements, the policyholder receives corresponding
indemnity, provided the orders in question were not already in force before the
insured event.

7.1.3 Price increases occurring between the insured event and reinstatement are
indemnified where reinstatement is secured within three years.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts of the insured property, and to those items
of insured property, that were themselves affected by the insured event. The
affected parts and items are the rooms, surfaces, building components and
appliances in which physical damage caused by the event is established by the
loss investigation - by inspection, by photographic record, or by technical
measurement taken at or shortly after the time of the loss.

Work carried out on a room, surface, component or item that was not itself
affected is not covered. This applies even where the work is carried out so that
repaired and unrepaired parts correspond in appearance or specification; for
reasons of convenience or economy; at the same time as covered work or in the
course of it; or by the same contractor as the covered work and invoiced
together with it.

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces and matched sets
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only where a corresponding
replacement material is no longer obtainable and a visible discontinuity would
otherwise remain. There is no corresponding entitlement in respect of sets,
suites, systems or assemblies of appliances: where one appliance of a set or
system was affected, indemnity is confined to that appliance and does not extend
to the remaining, undamaged appliances of the set or system, whatever the loss of
uniformity, compatibility or resale value.

7.1.7 Preparatory and ancillary work forming part of the repair
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) include taking down, dismantling and
disposing of the affected components; the drying and substrate preparation
necessary before the repair can be carried out; materials of a type, quality,
grade and specification corresponding to those in place immediately before the
insured event; and unaffected trim and edging elements that have to be taken off
to reach an affected component and cannot be refitted afterwards.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however
they may be described, bundled or invoiced, and irrespective of whether they
appear on an invoice that also contains covered work:

  (a) measures directed at the general condition, cleanliness, upkeep,
      modernisation or improvement of the insured property, as distinct from
      making good the damage caused by the insured event;

  (b) carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage, transport,
      logistics and comparable charges for bringing replacement property to the
      insured location, whether raised by the supplier of that property or by a
      third party, and whether stated as a separate line, as a percentage or as a
      flat rate;

  (c) fitting, mounting, installing, connecting, commissioning, setting up,
      calibrating, configuring, programming, pairing, demonstrating or
      instructing in the use of replacement property, and the removal or
      disposal of packaging arising from it. This applies whether the charge is
      raised by the supplier of the property or by a separate trade, and whether
      or not the original property had itself been installed;

  (d) call-out, travel, journey, mileage, vehicle, standby and comparable
      attendance charges, save where they are incurred on the occasion of, and
      on the same invoice as, work that is itself indemnifiable under these
      conditions; where the work billed on an invoice is not indemnifiable, the
      attendance charge on that invoice is not indemnifiable either. Where
      indemnifiable, one such charge per invoice and per attendance is
      reimbursed;

  (e) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to
      the repair - its own tools and consumable small equipment, its own
      diagnostic and measuring devices, provisioning for its own personnel, and
      general administrative, handling, order-processing or documentation charges
      levied in addition to itemised labour and materials;

  (f) charges arising from an arrangement of the kind described in 3.1.5, and
      charges relating to a liability risk of the kind described in 3.1.4,
      including any charge for raising, placing, registering or administering an
      order under such an arrangement;

  (g) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades;
      only the first such charge is indemnified.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, capability and
specification in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher
specification, a larger format, a superior material, a greater capacity or a
premium range is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an
equivalent standard-grade replacement corresponding to what was in place before
the loss; the difference is borne by the policyholder.

7.1.10 Evidence and apportionment
The policyholder demonstrates, for each item and each head of cost claimed, the
affected item to which it relates and the making-good purpose it serves. Where an
invoice line bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable elements without
separate pricing, and the split cannot be established from the documents, the
line is assessed by its predominant stated purpose. Where the predominant purpose

case.description:
During a thunderstorm a power surge came through the mains and damaged several pieces of the home entertainment setup that were plugged in and running - the TV, the speaker system and the AV receiver. A technician attended, produced a surge-failure report and checked the building wiring.

Nothing on that circuit was on a surge-protected strip. One of the mains plugs and its power lead were physically melted by the surge. The claim also lists the HDMI cables and remotes and the wall bracket.

A couple of items need flagging. The DVD player had already been playing up for months before the storm and is showing its age, and the router is on the claim but no diagnostic report was produced for it. The technician's invoice carries a return visit, a distribution-board wiring check, an admin fee and a separate call-out line.
